title: Latency-aware reservation mediator and soft-fill orchestrator
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally face oscillation between burst allocations and steady reservations when traffic includes short-lived spikes. Consequence: noisy autoscaler signals, excess preemption, and latency SLO degradation for high-priority tenants. This PR introduces a latency-aware reservation mediator that smooths reservation ramp-up and a soft-fill orchestrator that opportunistically fills warm pool capacity without violating throughput guarantees. Goals: 1) Reduce oscillation during sub-minute burst patterns. 2) Preserve tail latency SLOs for high-priority tenants while allowing low-priority opportunistic fill. 3) Emit detailed utilization and decision telemetry for post-mortem and tuning.
body:
Changeset summary and design notes:
- Introduces ReservationMediator (controller/orchestrator) responsible for gradual reservation increases, per-tenant ramp profiles, and latency feedback integration.
- Adds SoftFillOrchestrator that uses a soft agreement protocol to place opportunistic work in warm pools when headroom and predicted tail-latency budget allow.
- Introduces new telemetry: mediator_decision{tenant,decision,reason}, ramp_progress_pct, softfill_attempt{success|fail}, and headroom_predicted_margin.
- New config flags: --mediator-enabled, --mediator-default-ramp-ms, --softfill-strictness (0..10), and per-tenant ramp overrides via ReservationPolicy CRD.
- Safety: soft-fill is preemptible and gated by a fast latency check (p99 sliding window). If p99 breaches threshold, soft-fill drains immediately.
- Backwards compatibility: when mediator disabled, autoscaler behavior is unchanged. Soft-fill defaults to off in existing clusters.
- Rollout plan: feature flag off by default, gradual rollout to 5% of fleets, tuned against canary workloads before wider enablement.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4521)
- [x] Unit tests for mediator state machine
- [x] Integration test for soft-fill preemption path
- [x] Telemetry schema and Grafana dashboard skeleton
- [x] Feature flags and helm values

Related/context: This builds on prior autoscaler smoothing work but focuses on tenant-level latency feedback as a primary signal rather than pure utilization. See previous work items ENG-3984 and the telemetry notes in SUP-1182.

review_comments: Marcus Chen: Overall design looks sound, but we need clearer bounds on how ramp profiles interact with reservation decay. Please add explicit decay math and proof of no deadlock.
Aisha Patel: Added decay formula and unit tests in d2c8a8f. Also documented edge cases in mediator-rollout.md.
Riley Thompson: CI caught a race in headroom predictor on initial run; marked as blocking until fixed.
Aisha Patel: Fixed race by adding a read-lock around the predictor state; added integration test that reproduces previous failure.
Evan Morales: Telemetry names look good. Request: include a tag for per-pool vs per-tenant in metrics to help aggregation.
Aisha Patel: Updated telemetry to include pool_id and tenant_id labels; pushed change in c7e9f13.
Marcus Chen: Approving once CI flips green and docs have diffed dashboard screenshots.
ci_incidents: integration-tests initially failed due to headroom predictor race (fixed in f45a1b1). Rerun succeeded.
merge_details: Merged via squash (Aisha Patel) on 2026-03-04. Merge commit: squash of 6 commits. Release note: Introduced ReservationMediator and SoftFillOrchestrator for smoother reservation ramps and opportunistic warm pool utilization; opt-in via helm flags. Requires config review for tenants with tight tail latency requirements.
release_notes: Introduce latency-aware reservation mediator and soft-fill orchestrator. Feature gated: off by default. Adds new telemetry for tuning (mediator_decision, ramp_progress_pct, softfill_attempt, headroom_predicted_margin). Helm values to enable mediator and tune soft-fill strictness.
